props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the caller's element instead of a `<button>`, keeping every style and data attribute. This is how a button navigates without the library depending on a router: ```tsx <Button asChild><Link href="/pricing">Pricing</Link></Button> ``` A link that looks like a button must be an `<a>`, not a `<button>` with an onClick — otherwise middle-click, cmd-click, "open in new tab" and "copy link address" all break, and a screen reader announces the wrong role. `loading` and `disabled` are ignored when `asChild` is set: `disabled` is not a valid attribute on an anchor, and a spinner inside someone else's element would fight their children. props.description: `localStorage` key. Defaults to `'vk-theme'`. Must match the one in `themeScript`.

props.name: attribute
props.description: Attribute set on `<html>`. Defaults to `'data-theme'`, which is what tokens.css reads.

props.name: enableSystem
props.description: Set to `false` to reject a stored `'system'` and stay on an explicit theme.

components.title: Theme toggle
components.description: The theme switch every consumer asks for.

props.name: labels
props.description: Override the announced label for the theme the press would move TO.

props.name: 'aria-label'
props.description: Overrides the derived label entirely.

components.title: Time picker
components.description: A time field made of spinbutton segments — hours, minutes, optional seconds, optional AM/PM — rather than a free-text box or a scrolling list of every quarter hour.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value, always in 24-hour form: `'HH:mm'`, or `'HH:mm:ss'` with `withSeconds`. `null` while any required segment is empty. The 12-hour display never leaks into the value — `hourCycle` is presentation, the canonical string is the data.

props.name: withSeconds
props.description: Add a seconds segment. Default `false`.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description: `24` (default) or `12` with an AM/PM segment. Deterministic on purpose: `Intl` would pick per machine, and a field that shows 24-hour to the server and 12-hour to the browser is a hydration mismatch waiting to happen. Choose it for your audience.

props.name: min
props.description: Inclusive bounds in the same canonical form. A committed value is clamped into them.

props.name: name
props.description: One hidden field carrying the canonical value, so a form never sees the segments.

components.title: Timeline
components.description: Compound component: `Timeline` and `Timeline.Item`.

props.name: align
props.description: `start` (default) keeps every entry on one side of the rail. `alternate` zig-zags them, and falls back to `start` on a container too narrow to hold two columns — so it is safe to set unconditionally.

components.title: Toast
components.description: One notification. `ToastProvider` renders these for you, but it is exported so a static toast can be dropped into a docs page or a form's inline slot.

props.name: title
props.description: Bold leading line.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary line under the title.

props.name: action
props.description: A control the toast offers — typically a `<Button size="sm">Undo</Button>`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph. Pass `null` to drop the default.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called when the dismiss button is pressed. Its presence is what renders the button.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the dismiss button.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: `false` hides the dismiss button even when `onDismiss` is given.

components.title: Tooltip
components.description: A description that appears on hover and on focus.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger. Exactly one element, and it must spread the props it is given - `aria-describedby` has to land on the real interactive element for a screen reader to read the tip, and a wrapper `<span>` cannot stand in for it. A ref is attached to it (composed with any ref it already had) to measure against, with the first pointer or focus event as a fallback - so a child that swallows refs still positions correctly on hover.

props.name: content
props.description: The tip. Keep it short and non-interactive: a tooltip is never focusable.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side. Flipped to its opposite when there is no room. Default `'top'`.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment. Default `'center'`.

props.name: offset
props.description: Gap between trigger and tip, px. Default `8`.

props.name: padding
props.description: Minimum distance kept from the viewport edges, px. Default `8`.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state while uncontrolled. Default `false`.

props.name: openDelay
props.description: Delay before a hover opens the tip, ms. Default `200`. Keyboard focus deliberately ignores this and opens immediately: a delay on hover stops tips flickering as the pointer crosses a toolbar, but a keyboard user has already committed by pressing Tab, and making them wait is just lag.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: Delay before the tip closes after the pointer leaves, ms. Default `150`. Must stay above zero: it is the window in which the pointer can cross the gap from the trigger onto the tip itself without the tip disappearing underneath it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Never open. For a trigger whose tip is temporarily meaningless.

props.name: container
props.description: Where to portal the tip. Defaults to `document.body`.

components.title: Typing indicator
components.description: Three animated dots meaning "a reply is coming".

props.name: label
props.description: Announced text. Defaults to `Assistant is typing`.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Also show the label on screen. Off by default: the dots carry the meaning.

props.name: dots
props.description: How many dots. Defaults to 3.

props.name: active
props.description: When `false` the live region stays mounted but empty. Use this when you want a guaranteed announcement — see the accessibility note on the component.

components.title: Video player
components.description: A video player with its own controls — progressive files (MP4, WebM), no streaming.

props.name: src
props.description: One URL, or several sources the browser tries **in order**. List the most widely supported format first (MP4/H.264, then WebM): Safari holds the document's `load` event while it works through a format it cannot decode, so a WebM-first list makes the whole page appear to hang there.

props.name: poster
props.description: Frame shown before playback. **A raster image (JPEG, PNG, WebP)** — Safari ignores an SVG poster, and the document's `load` event never fires while it waits for one.

props.name: tracks
props.description: WebVTT text tracks. The first `default` one (else the first) is the captions track.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the player. Default `'Video player'`.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Width / height. Default `16 / 9`.

props.name: muted
props.description: Start muted — required by every browser for `autoPlay` to actually play.

props.name: playsInline
props.description: Default `true`: play in place on phones instead of taking over the screen.

props.name: rates
props.description: Playback speeds offered. Default `[0.5, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2]`; `[]` hides the control.

props.name: seekStep
props.description: Seconds moved by ArrowLeft / ArrowRight. Default `5`.

props.name: hideControlsAfter
props.description: Hide the controls this many ms after the pointer rests while playing. `0` never hides. Default `2500`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown when the media fails to load or decode.

props.name: videoRef
props.description: The `<video>` element, for anything the props do not cover.

props.name: videoProps
props.description: Extra attributes for the `<video>` — `crossOrigin` for cross-origin captions, for one.

components.title: Virtual list
components.description: Windowed list: renders only the rows on screen.

props.name: items
props.description: The full dataset. Only the visible slice is ever rendered.

props.name: itemHeight
props.description: Row height in pixels. A number means every row is that tall, which is the fast path: the scroll position maps to an index with one division and nothing needs measuring. A function is the estimate for a row whose real height is not known yet. Rows are measured as they render and the estimate is replaced, so a wrong estimate costs accuracy in the scrollbar early on, not correctness.

props.name: children
props.description: Renders one row. Must not itself be tall enough to scroll.

props.name: overscan
props.description: Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport. Default `4`. Zero is tempting and wrong: the browser paints scrolled-in rows a frame late, which reads as a flicker of blank space at speed.

props.name: getKey
props.description: Stable key for a row. Strongly recommended — see the note on the default below.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the scrollable region.

props.name: scrollToIndex
props.description: Scroll this index into view whenever it changes.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fired with the visible range whenever it changes. Useful for infinite loading.

charts.title: AreaChart
charts.description: A line chart with the region under each series filled. The y axis always includes zero, because an area measured from an arbitrary floor overstates its own magnitude.

props.name: data
props.description: Single series. `[{ x, y }]`, or a bare `number[]` where the index is the x.

props.name: series
props.description: Multiple series. Takes precedence over `data` when both are given.

props.name: interactiveLegend
props.description: Each legend entry is a checkbox that shows and hides its series, with a fade — the way every charting library's users expect a legend to behave. On by default whenever the legend shows; pass `false` for a figure in a report, where the legend is a key and not a control. No JavaScript and no client boundary: the entries are real checkboxes and the chart reacts with `:has()`.

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stack the series on top of one another instead of overlaying them. Positive and negative values stack in opposite directions from zero, so mixed signs still read.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Opt in to the pointer hover tooltip. Mouse only - the data table is the AT path.

charts.title: BarChart
charts.description: Vertical or horizontal bars, grouped or stacked, in pure SVG. The value axis always includes zero - a bar chart that starts anywhere else misrepresents its own data - and negative bars extend the other side of the zero line.

props.name: data
props.description: Single series. `[{ x, y }]`, or a bare `number[]` where the index is the x.

props.name: series
props.description: Multiple series. Takes precedence over `data` when both are given.

props.name: interactiveLegend
props.description: Each legend entry is a checkbox that shows and hides its series, with a fade — the way every charting library's users expect a legend to behave. On by default whenever the legend shows; pass `false` for a figure in a report, where the legend is a key and not a control. No JavaScript and no client boundary: the entries are real checkboxes and the chart reacts with `:has()`.

props.name: mode
props.description: `grouped` puts a series side by side inside each category; `stacked` piles them, with negatives stacking downward from zero.

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Bars run left to right, with the categories down the left edge.

props.name: barRadius
props.description: Corner radius, in viewBox px. Clamped so short bars do not turn into lozenges.

props.name: categoryPadding
props.description: Fraction of each category slot left empty, 0 to 0.9.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print each value at the end of its bar - the clearest non-colour cue there is.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Pointer hover tooltip. Mouse only, and ignored for `horizontal`.

charts.title: Gauge
charts.description: A gauge — one value against a bounded scale, with optional threshold bands.

props.name: bands
props.description: Threshold bands under the arc — the "green / amber / red" zones a dashboard gauge exists for. Without bands the track is a single neutral arc.

props.name: diameter
props.description: Diameter of the `viewBox`, in px. The chart scales to its container width.

props.name: thickness
props.description: Arc thickness in px.

props.name: caption
props.description: Text under the value, e.g. a unit.

charts.title: Heatmap
charts.description: A matrix heatmap — two categorical axes, intensity for the value.

props.name: columns
props.description: Explicit column order. Also renders columns that have no data yet.

props.name: rows
props.description: Explicit row order. Also renders rows that have no data yet.

props.name: min
props.description: Intensity scale bounds. Default to the data's own extent.

props.name: color
props.description: Base colour of the ramp. Any CSS colour; defaults to the first chart token. The ramp runs from the surface colour to this, so it holds in both themes without a second palette — intensity is mixed in the browser with `color-mix`.

props.name: cellSize
props.description: Height of one row in px. Cells are square-ish; width divides evenly.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Print each value inside its cell. Off above 5% of cells being 4+ characters wide.

charts.title: LineChart
charts.description: A multi-series line chart in pure SVG - no d3, no canvas, nothing measured, so it renders complete on the server.

props.name: data
props.description: Single series. `[{ x, y }]`, or a bare `number[]` where the index is the x.

props.name: series
props.description: Multiple series. Takes precedence over `data` when both are given.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the `viewBox`, in px. The chart scales to its container width.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Defaults to on for more than one series.

props.name: interactiveLegend
props.description: Each legend entry is a checkbox that shows and hides its series, with a fade — the way every charting library's users expect a legend to behave. On by default whenever the legend shows; pass `false` for a figure in a report, where the legend is a key and not a control. No JavaScript and no client boundary: the entries are real checkboxes and the chart reacts with `:has()`.

props.name: showPoints
props.description: Per-point markers. Defaults to on while every series has 24 points or fewer.

props.name: curve
props.description: `smooth` draws a Catmull-Rom spline; control points are clamped to the plot.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Opt in to the pointer hover tooltip. Mouse only - the data table is the AT path.

charts.title: PieChart
charts.description: A pie or donut chart in pure SVG. Non-positive and non-finite slices are dropped - they have no meaning in a part-to-whole picture - and the remaining values are normalised, so slices always add up to the circle.

props.name: data
props.description: Slices, in drawing order (clockwise from 12 o clock).

props.name: donut
props.description: Punch out the middle.

props.name: innerRadius
props.description: Hole diameter as a fraction of the outer radius, `0` to `0.95`. Only applies with `donut`; defaults to `0.6`.

props.name: diameter
props.description: Rendered diameter in pixels. Named `diameter`, not `size`, because `size` is a sm/md/lg scale everywhere else in the library — same word, different type, was a trap.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Show the legend. Defaults to `true`. Note there is deliberately no `interactiveLegend` here, unlike LineChart, AreaChart and BarChart. A pie shows parts of a whole, and hiding one wedge would leave a gap while the rest kept their original angles - so the chart would no longer sum to 100% and would quietly misreport every remaining share. Re-proportioning needs the geometry recomputed, which CSS cannot do. Use a BarChart when series need to be toggled.

props.name: showLabels
props.description: Percentage inside each slice. Slices under 4% are skipped, as they cannot fit.

props.name: startAngle
props.description: Degrees clockwise from 12 o clock for the first slice.

props.name: padAngle
props.description: Gap between slices, in degrees.

props.name: centerLabel
props.description: Big text in the middle of a donut, e.g. the total.

props.name: centerSublabel
props.description: Smaller text under `centerLabel`.

charts.title: ProgressRing
charts.description: A circular determinate progress indicator: one SVG circle with a dash offset, which is why it needs no path maths, no measurement and no client JS.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. Out-of-range and non-finite input is clamped, never NaN.

props.name: diameter
props.description: Rendered diameter in pixels. Named `diameter`, not `size`, because `size` is a sm/md/lg scale everywhere else in the library — same word, different type, was a trap.

props.name: thickness
props.description: Stroke width in px. Clamped so it can never exceed the radius.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name, e.g. "Storage used".

props.name: showValue
props.description: Percentage in the middle of the ring.

props.name: children
props.description: Arbitrary centre content, e.g. a big number over a caption. Wins over `showValue`.

props.name: color
props.description: Any CSS colour for the filled arc. Defaults to the `--vk-chart-1` token.

props.name: trackColor
props.description: Any CSS colour for the unfilled track.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the centre percentage. Must be locale-stable to stay hydration-safe.

props.name: startAngle
props.description: Degrees clockwise from 12 o clock where the arc begins.

props.name: square
props.description: Square off the arc ends.

props.name: title
props.description: SVG `<title>` for the graphic.

charts.title: RadarChart
charts.description: A radar chart — several measures of one thing, drawn as a polygon per series.

props.name: data
props.description: Single series: one value per axis, in axis order.

props.name: series
props.description: Multiple series. Takes precedence over `data` when both are given.

props.name: axes
props.description: Axis names, clockwise from the top. Values beyond the axis count are dropped.

props.name: max
props.description: Top of the scale. Defaults to the largest value across every series.

props.name: diameter
props.description: Diameter of the `viewBox`, in px. The chart scales to its container width.

props.name: rings
props.description: Concentric guide rings.

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill each polygon with a translucent wash.

props.name: interactiveLegend
props.description: Each legend entry is a checkbox that shows and hides its series, with a fade — the way every charting library's users expect a legend to behave. On by default whenever the legend shows; pass `false` for a figure in a report, where the legend is a key and not a control. No JavaScript and no client boundary: the entries are real checkboxes and the chart reacts with `:has()`.

charts.title: ScatterChart
charts.description: A scatter chart — and, the moment any point carries `r`, a bubble chart. One component for both because they are one picture: position encodes the relationship, and `r` optionally encodes a third measure.

props.name: data
props.description: Single series.

props.name: series
props.description: Multiple series. Takes precedence over `data` when both are given.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the `viewBox`, in px. The chart scales to its container width.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Defaults to on for more than one series.

props.name: interactiveLegend
props.description: Each legend entry is a checkbox that shows and hides its series, with a fade — the way every charting library's users expect a legend to behave. On by default whenever the legend shows; pass `false` for a figure in a report, where the legend is a key and not a control. No JavaScript and no client boundary: the entries are real checkboxes and the chart reacts with `:has()`.

props.name: markSize
props.description: Mark radius in px when no point carries `r`.

props.name: maxBubbleSize
props.description: Largest bubble radius in px, reached by the largest `r` in the data.

charts.title: Sparkline
charts.description: A tiny, axis-free trend line meant to sit inside a sentence, a table cell or a stat card. Pure SVG, no measurement, no dependencies.

props.name: data
props.description: The trend. Non-finite entries are dropped before anything is drawn.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the internal coordinate space, in px. Default `32`.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the internal coordinate space. The sparkline stretches to fill its container, so this only sets the aspect ratio the geometry is designed against.

props.name: stroke
props.description: Any CSS colour. Defaults to the `--vk-chart-1` token.

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill under the line: `true` for a tint of `stroke`, or an explicit CSS colour.

props.name: showLastPoint
props.description: Dot on the final value - the "where are we now" cue.

props.name: accessibleTable
props.description: Visually hidden `<table>` of the values. On by default.
